‘’’Herant A. Katchadourian’’’ (born January 23, 1933) is an Armenian-American psychiatrist and professor. He was born in Turkey and raised in [[Beirut]]. He was a [[Dean (education)|Dean]] at Stanford University, and a [[Professor]] of Human Biology.<ref name=":2">P. F. Sommerfeldt, “[http://www.electrummagazine.com/2014/06/odyssey-from-iskenderun-to-beirut-to-america-an-extraordinary-memoir Odyssey from Iskenderun to Beirut to America: An Extraordinary Memoir, in 'The Way It Turned Out']“; ‘’Electrum Magazine’’, June 5, 2014; accessed 2019.10.26</ref> He became renowned in the late 20th Century as an pioneering author and instructor of human sexuality.<ref name = AUB /> In later life, he served as trustee of many organizations. He is the father of artist [[Nina Katchadourian]].

== Early life ==
Herant Aram Katchadourian was born on January 23, 1933, in [[İskenderun]], Turkey. His parents were Aram Adour and Efronia (Nazarian) Katchadourian. He earned a Bachelor’s degree at the [[American University of Beirut]] in 1954, and a Doctor of Medicine, also from American University, Beirut, in 1958. He did postgraduate work in psychiatry at the [[University of Rochester]], finishing in 1961.<ref name = "AUB">“[https://www.aub.edu.lb/AboutUs/bot/emeriti/Pages/katchadourian.aspx Herant Katchadourian, MD]“, American University of Beirut; accessed 2026.05.17.</ref> He is fluent in five languages.<ref name = :2 />
Katchadourian immigrated to the United States in 1958. He was naturalized as a citizen in 1972.

== Career ==
Katchadourian arrived at [[Stanford University]] in 1966.<ref>“[https://stanfordmag.org/contents/guilty Guilty!]“ ‘’Stanford Magazine’’, Nov.-Dec. 2009; accessed 2026.05.17.</ref> He became a professor of psychiatry and behavioral sciences as well as human biology. He also served as university ombudsman, vice provost, and dean of undergraduate studies.<ref name = SUA>“[https://oac.cdlib.org/findaid/ark:/13030/kt1k4035d1 Katchadourian (Herant A.) Papers, 1951-2006]“, Stanford University Archives; accessed 2026.05.17.</ref>

In 1968, Katchadourian began teaching Stanford’s class in Human Sexuality, Human Biology 10.<ref name = "SD">Angelique Dakkak, “[https://stanforddaily.com/2014/02/13/qa-professor-katchadourian-talks-hookup-culture/ Q&A: Professor Katchadourian talks hookup culture]“, ‘’The Stanford Daily’’, Feb. 13, 2014; accessed 2026.05.19.</ref> It became known as “the most heavily subscribed class in the history of the university”; over 20,000 students took the course before Katchadourian stopped teaching it in 2002. At its peak, one-quarter of Stanford’s undergraduate students were enrolled in the class.<ref>“[https://stanfordmag.org/contents/everything-they-wanted-to-know-and-often-asked Everything They Wanted to Know, and Often Asked]“, ‘’Stanford Magazine’’, Sep./Oct. 2012; accessed 2026.05.19.</ref>

As time passed, the scope of the course expanded to include additional topics such as sexual orientation, sexually-transmissible diseases, date rape, and harassment.<ref name = SD /> Katchadourian wrote and subsequently expanded the textbook, ‘’Fundamentals of Human Sexuality’’,<ref>Herant A. Katchadourian and Donald T. Lunde, ‘’Fundamentals of Human Sexuality’’, New York: Holt, Rinehart & Winston, 1972.</ref> which went through numerous editions and revisions.<ref>Herant A. Katchadourian and Donald T. Lunde, ‘’Fundamentals of Human Sexuality’’, second edition, New York: Holt, Rinehart & Winston, 1975.</ref><ref>Herant A. Katchadourian, ‘’Fundamentals of Human Sexuality’’, fourth edition, New York: Holt, Rinehart & Winston, 1985.</ref><ref>Herant A. Katchadourian, ‘’Fundamentals of Human Sexuality’’, fifth edition, 1989.</ref>

Katchadourian became a trustee of his ‘’alma mater’’, American University of Beirut, in 2001, retiring in 2008. He was also a trustee of [[Haigazian University]], a trustee of the [[William and Flora Hewlett Foundation]], and president of the Flora Family Foundation.<ref name = AUB />.

==Personal life==
Katchadourian married Stina Lindfors, a literary translator and writer from Finland,<ref>Julia Klein, “A Closer Look”, ‘’Brown Alumni Magazine’’, March 2009; accessed 2019.03.06.</ref> in 1964. They have two children, [[Nina Katchadourian|Nina]] and Kai.

==Bibliography==
Works by Katchadourian include:

*’’Fundamentals of Human Sexuality’’ (1972)
*’’Human Sexuality: Sense and Nonsense’’ (1974)
*’’Biological Aspects of Human Sexuality’’ (1975)
*’’The Biology of Adolescence’’ (1977)
*’’Human Sexuality: A Comparative and Developmental Perspective’’ (1979)
*’’La sexualidad humana: un estudio comparativo de su evolución’’ (1983)
*’’Careerism and Intellectualism Among College Students’’ (Jossey Bass Higher and Adult Education Series) (1985)
*’’Midlife in perspective: 50’’ (1986)
*’’Cream of the Crop: The Impact of Elite Education in the Decade After College’’ (1994)
*’’The Developing Adult: Biological & Psychosocial Perspectives’’ (1996)
*’’Guilt: The Bite of Conscience’’ (2009) 
*’’The Way It Turned Out: A Memoir’’ (2012)
